verdict.rationale: Orama documents incremental document insertion, including batched insertMultiple, in the JS library. In Orama Cloud, data sources are segregated so you can update, delete, or add data without affecting other sources, which points to incremental changes rather than full rebuilds. Missing for 10: explicit per-document update/delete APIs in the evidence, any stated near-real-time visibility or indexing latency, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, document adds, updates, and deletes become searchable in near real time without a full reindex

citations.quote: Every data source is segregated from the others, so you can update, delete, or add new data without affecting the data in the other data sources.
insertion in Orama is quick and intuitive
If you have a lot of records, we suggest using the insertMultiple function... You can pass a third, optional, parameter to change the batch size (default: 1000).
you can put data that will be updated frequently in a single data source (let's call it `docs`), and put data that follows a different update schedule in another data source
